nodes.label: Exact Body selector namespace
nodes.rationale: Only variables in the component collection whose names start with case sensitive body/ form the visible product token interface. Body in another position or collection, including section-header, table and characters body roles, is excluded.

nodes.label: Hidden internal tokens remain functional
nodes.rationale: All non Body variables use empty scopes where Figma accepts them, including primitive, semantic and component family tokens. Empty scopes filter selectors without deleting aliases, breaking bindings, converting values to literals or changing publishing visibility; official components retain their own component to semantic to primitive chains.

nodes.label: Function specific Body selector scopes
nodes.rationale: The 33 existing Body tokens use TEXT_FILL for text colors, FRAME_FILL and SHAPE_FILL for backgrounds, FONT_FAMILY for family, FONT_STYLE for current STRING weights, FONT_SIZE, LINE_HEIGHT, LETTER_SPACING, GAP for both gap and padding, and CORNER_RADIUS. ALL_SCOPES and ALL_FILLS are excluded; current STRING weights are not converted to numeric weights.

nodes.label: Future token visibility declaration gate
nodes.rationale: Each future component/body token must declare name, type, function and only necessary compatible scopes in delegated JSON; an undeclared Body role blocks generation and QA. All other new tokens and families start with empty scopes. Conditional border, sizing, numeric weight, opacity, effect and paragraph mappings do not create or expose new tokens.

nodes.label: Scope correction preservation boundary
nodes.rationale: The correction preserves variable and collection identity, descriptions, modes and ordering, mode values, aliases, codeSyntax, bindings and publication visibility, plus all five Body typography styles and links. It changes variable metadata without editing canvas, component visuals or styles, and creates no composition or component.

nodes.label: Effective scope overlay preserves historical sources
nodes.rationale: Delegated visibility correction applies after token inventories and amendments in web-inputs and overrides effective scopes only. The generator validates the whole inventory and records the overlay in its manifest; historical snapshot bytes and CSS variables remain intact, so effective consumption must include the overlay or generated manifest.

nodes.label: TOKEN QA 03 visibility and preservation acceptance
nodes.rationale: Every token or component addition or correction runs TOKEN-QA-03 with QA-01 and QA-02: reread exact compatible Body scopes and empty internal scopes; compare preserved fields, all-page binding and paint fingerprints, explicit modes, style references, invisible and nested nodes, and five complete Body styles. Web checks effective manifest, themed chains and unchanged CSS for scope-only corrections.

nodes.label: Visibility validation by observed variable type
nodes.rationale: API scope rejections must be recorded by type without altering function, values or publishing. Current inventory contains COLOR, FLOAT and STRING but no BOOLEAN, so BOOLEAN is not claimed tested; any future type requires explicit validation and limits universal visibility claims until resolved.

nodes.label: Binding validity separated from selector scopes
nodes.rationale: TOKEN-QA-01 checks variable type and semantic role against actual consumption. Empty scopes are mandatory for internal tokens and do not invalidate a compatible binding; selector availability cannot replace type, alias-chain and role validation.

nodes.label: Mandatory TOKEN QA 03 for Figma and web
nodes.rationale: The protocol requires visibility QA on every token or component addition or correction: exact component/body namespace and compatible declared scopes, empty internal scopes, readback preservation and effective web manifest. New families remain hidden, historical scopes remain observed evidence, and the current correction controls effective consumption.

nodes.label: Visibility documentary delegation boundary
nodes.rationale: Documentary QA accepts the exact component/body prefix, empty internal scopes, preserved identity, aliases, bindings, Body styles and publication. Canonical JSON is SHA-256 fixed and changes no values or descriptions. Namespace, selector versus binding and publication distinctions are explicit; implementation is delegated without publication, installation or family redesign.

nodes.label: Visibility correction readback result
nodes.rationale: Figma changed only scopes to empty on 1098 internal variables; 331 were already hidden and 33 Body scopes stayed specific. Final local inventory has 33 visible and 1429 hidden of 1462 variables, with no canvas edit or library publication.

nodes.label: Visibility preservation evidence across all pages
nodes.rationale: Before and after inventories preserve all authorized fields except scopes, 4643 alias values, 1123 component and 151 semantic token chains, 188 primitive values and five Body styles. Matching SHA-256 fingerprints cover 43 pages and 19692 nodes including nested instances and invisible layers; visual screenshots do not substitute for real binding evidence.

nodes.label: Effective manifest and unchanged CSS verification
nodes.rationale: The effective manifest exposes scopes only for 33 Body tokens out of 1462 while historical source snapshots stay unchanged. CSS retains the same SHA-256; generator and 50-family checks pass. The visibility checker covers namespace boundaries, other collections, case sensitivity, undeclared Body roles and ALL_SCOPES rejection.

nodes.label: Observed empty scope type compatibility
nodes.rationale: Readback confirms COLOR, FLOAT and STRING accepted empty scopes. BOOLEAN is absent and is not claimed tested. GAP covers padding and gap, and publishing visibility remains preserved instead of being used to hide tokens from selectors.

nodes.label: Selector policy in component consumption rules
nodes.rationale: Design rules restrict visible selectors to exact body/ names inside component with functional scopes and empty scopes elsewhere. Body serves custom product content, official component aliases and bindings remain internal, and every addition or correction must pass TOKEN-QA-03 without changing publication.

nodes.label: Registered effective visibility correction
nodes.rationale: The contract registry records FOUNDATIONS-TOKEN-VISIBILITY-001 as a delegated effective-scope correction after documentary QA, exposing only component/body as product interface without changing family versions.

nodes.label: Registered Body only selector implementation
nodes.rationale: Implementation registry records 1098 corrected scopes, 33 visible Body variables, 1429 hidden internal variables and a web manifest overlay with unchanged CSS, linking full QA evidence and excluding publishing or installation.

nodes.label: Registered visibility and preservation QA
nodes.rationale: Registry records passing documentary and implementation QA and mandatory TOKEN-QA-03 for every addition or correction in Figma and web. Scope, alias, value, binding, Body-style and publishing comparisons cover 1462 variables, 43 pages and 19692 nodes.

nodes.label: Visibility correction provenance
nodes.rationale: SRC-TOKEN-VISIBILITY-20261117 fixes the explicit user request and canonical scope JSON by SHA-256, retaining before and after Figma readings without replacing historical token values or aliases.

nodes.label: Figma consumer guide visibility correction
nodes.rationale: The skill reads the visibility contract and canonical overlay from the verified design-system snapshot. It exposes exact component/body only for product content, preserves internal component tokens, Body styles and aliases despite empty scopes, and requires TOKEN-QA-03 readback without ALL_SCOPES or hiddenFromPublishing changes.

nodes.label: Prototype consumer guide effective token visibility
nodes.rationale: The prototype skill consumes the effective manifest or overlays canonical scopes on historical inventories. Only exact component/body is a product token interface; official component tokens must not be replaced by Body, semantic tokens or literals. CSS variables, modes, Body styles and bindings remain preserved and QA-03 applies in Figma and web without publishing or installation.

nodes.label: Variables foundation effective scope amendment
nodes.rationale: The foundation preserves historical JSON bytes, hash and provenance while the visibility correction overrides only effective scopes. Only component/body is exposed with specific scopes; all other variables retain function with empty scopes and unchanged identity, aliases, values, bindings and publication.

nodes.label: Body foundation selector interface amendment
nodes.rationale: Body architecture now delegates effective scopes to the visibility policy: only the exact body/ prefix in component appears on compatible selectors. Other tokens remain functional internal dependencies, and consumers preserve Body styles and bindings while reading the canonical correction alongside historical inventory.
